chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who entered into Ihram for Umrah and forgot to shorten his prayer until Hajj entered, he said: 'He seeks Allah's forgiveness and there is no penalty upon him, and his Umrah is complete.'
And as for what is obligatory of the saying from the Talbiyah and what is recommended, it is what has been narrated:

key_terms.وَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: And there is no penalty upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to shorten prayers during Umrah?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that forgetting to shorten prayers during Umrah does not invalidate the ritual, reflecting the Shia principle of *al-akhthar* (taking the easier option) in cases of unintentional error. The hadith distinguishes between obligatory and recommended aspects of the pilgrimage, noting that while the Talbiyah is recommended, its specific recitation rules are detailed elsewhere, emphasizing the flexibility inherent in Shia fiqh for minor omissions.
